title: The 2-Adic Flux Towers over the 16-Cell: Jacobians Where the Group Ring Does Not Split
content: The eight units modulo \(30\) are the vertices of the 16-cell, and the 16-cell is the Cayley graph of \(U(30) = (\mathbb{Z}/30)^\times\) with respect to the six units that are not \(\pm 1\).  We study the \(\mathbb{Z}_2\)-towers of voltage covers \(Y_n(a,b)\) of this graph, in which the generators \(7\) and \(17\) carry a flux \((a,b)\) with \(a+b\) odd.  For odd \(p\) the group ring \(\mathbb{Z}_p[U(30)]\) splits into character components, and the \(p\)-part of the Jacobians can be read off component by component.  At \(p=2\) this fails, because \(U(30)\) is a \(2\)-group: \(3\) and \(5\) are Fermat primes.  We prove by hand that \[ \operatorname{Jac}(Y_n(a,b)) \otimes \mathbb{Z}_2 \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2^{n-1})^6 \oplus (\mathbb{Z}/2^{n+2})^5 \oplus (\mathbb{Z}/2^{n+4})^4 \] for every \(n \ge 2\) and every flux.  The proof has four steps.  The Iwasawa module of the tower is cyclic over \(\mathbb{Z}_2[C_4][[T]]\).  Modulo \(2\) it is \((\mathbb{F}_2[[T]]/T^4)^4\) for every flux.  From level \(2\) on, all elementary divisors double from one level to the next.  At level \(2\) the relation becomes twice an explicit element \(\rho\) of \(\mathbb{Z}[C_4 \times C_4]\), and the \(16 \times 16\) matrix of multiplication by \(\rho\) reduces by hand to two \(4 \times 4\) circulants.  As consequences, \(v_2\) of the number of spanning trees is \(15n+20\), the Iwasawa invariants are \(\mu=0\), \(\lambda=15\), \(\nu=20\), and nothing depends on the flux.  We also determine the first level by hand: \(\operatorname{Jac}(Y_1) \otimes \mathbb{Z}_2 \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2)^2 \oplus \mathbb{Z}/8 \oplus (\mathbb{Z}/16)^2 \oplus (\mathbb{Z}/32)^2\), which does not fit the pattern of the higher levels.  A companion script checks the main theorem by exact computation for all levels \(2 \le n \le 7\), in two independent runs.
